_doc: Service-specific working knowledge merged into data/services/_meta/{slug}.json by scripts/merge-service-knowledge.mjs. General professional practice drawn from CDC environmental infection control guidance, OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030, EPA label requirements and the facility-type guidance named on each service page. No statistics, no client claims.

highTouchZones: exam table surface and paper-roll holder
blood pressure cuffs and wall-mounted diagnostic sets
computer keyboards, mice and wall-mounted screens
sink faucet handles and soap dispensers
restroom flush handles, grab bars and door locks
protocolSteps: Agree the room-by-room scope and who disinfects patient-contact surfaces between visits.
Start each visit in the cleanest areas (offices, consult rooms) and finish in restrooms and soiled utility.
Clean visibly soiled surfaces before disinfecting; the label claim assumes a pre-cleaned surface.
Apply an EPA-registered hospital disinfectant and keep each surface wet for its full label contact time.
Change cloths between rooms using a color-coded system so restroom cloths never reach exam rooms.
Empty trash and recycling; leave sharps containers and regulated medical waste to your licensed hauler.
Damp-mop hard floors and vacuum carpeted waiting areas with HEPA-filtered equipment.
Record rooms completed, products used and any issues in the service log.
documentationDeliverables: product list with EPA registration numbers and contact times
Safety Data Sheets for every product on site
signed service logs for each visit
OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens training records for assigned staff
certificate of insurance naming the practice
ATP or fluorescent-marker results when verification is performed
frequencyGuide: Exam rooms: patient-contact surfaces between patients (usually clinical staff); full clean daily.
Waiting room and check-in: high-touch points several times a day in busy clinics, full clean daily.
Restrooms: at least daily, more often in high-volume practices.
Floors: daily damp-mop of hard floors; carpet vacuumed daily and extracted on a periodic schedule.
Walls, vents and light fixtures: on a periodic schedule or when visibly soiled.
vendorQuestions: Who on your team will actually clean our office, and what training records can you show for them?
Which disinfectants will you use, and what are their contact times?
How do you keep restroom cloths out of exam rooms?
What do you leave for our clinical staff, and what do you own?
What will our logs look like if a surveyor asks?
How do you handle a blood spill found during your visit?
Can you verify cleaning with ATP or fluorescent markers?
Who do we call if something is missed?
scheduleNotes: Most medical offices are cleaned after the last patient leaves, so exam rooms are ready for the first morning appointment.
Practices with early clinics often prefer an evening clean plus a short midday restroom and waiting-room refresh.

highTouchZones: delivery unit, tray and bracket table
X-ray tube head and sensor holder
keyboards and mice in each operatory
sterilization-area counters on the clean side
protocolSteps: Confirm which clinical contact surfaces and barriers your dental assistants handle between patients.
Keep the sterilization area's clean and dirty sides separate: separate cloths, clean side first, never back again.
Clean housekeeping surfaces — floors, walls, counters outside the operatory field — with an EPA-registered disinfectant.
Wipe operatory surfaces that are not barrier-protected at end of day, following the practice's product choice.
Leave dental unit waterlines, suction traps and instrument reprocessing to trained clinical staff.
Empty general trash; amalgam, sharps and regulated waste stay with your licensed hauler.
Damp-mop operatory floors, working from the back of the room toward the door.
Log each operatory, the products used and anything that needs the practice's attention.
documentationDeliverables: product list with EPA registration numbers and contact times
Safety Data Sheets for every product
bloodborne pathogen training records for assigned staff
certificate of insurance naming the practice
frequencyGuide: Clinical contact surfaces: between patients by the dental team (or barrier change).
Operatories and sterilization area housekeeping surfaces: daily after the last patient.
Floors: daily in operatories and the sterilization area.
Waiting room and restrooms: daily, with high-touch points more often in busy practices.
Walls, vents and cabinet exteriors: periodically or when visibly soiled.
vendorQuestions: How will your crew keep the clean and dirty sides of our sterilization area separate?
What will you never touch in the operatory?
Which products will you use near our dental equipment finishes?
How do you handle an aerosol-heavy day in terms of end-of-day cleaning?
What logs will we have for a Board of Registration in Dentistry inspection?
Who holds bloodborne pathogen training on your crew?
scheduleNotes: Dental offices are almost always cleaned after the last patient so the end-of-day clean reflects that day's aerosol exposure.
Practices with Saturday hours usually need a weekend visit or an early Monday clean.

highTouchZones: pulse oximeters and blood pressure cuffs
protocolSteps: Agree how rooms are turned between patients and what staff disinfect during hours.
Use disinfectants with contact times short enough for the room-turn pace your clinic runs.
Terminal-clean rooms used for patients with suspected contact-transmitted or respiratory infections as your policy requires.
Clean and disinfect the waiting room's shared surfaces — it holds the most undiagnosed patients.
Change cloths between rooms, clean to dirty, and never carry restroom equipment into exam rooms.
Empty trash; sharps and regulated waste stay with your licensed hauler.
Damp-mop floors throughout, including under stretchers and exam tables.
Log each room, product and time so the next shift knows what was done.
documentationDeliverables: product list with EPA registration numbers and contact times
frequencyGuide: Exam rooms: patient-contact surfaces between patients during hours, full clean at end of day.
Isolation or respiratory rooms: terminal clean after use as policy directs.
Waiting room: shared surfaces several times a day during peak hours.
Restrooms: several times a day in busy centers.
Floors: daily, with spot cleaning of spills immediately.
vendorQuestions: Can your products meet our room-turn time without shortening contact times?
How do you handle a room used by a patient with suspected C. difficile or norovirus?
Will you clean our waiting room during open hours, or only after close?
How do you coordinate with our staff on isolation rooms?
What do our logs look like at the end of each day?
scheduleNotes: Urgent care centers with long daily hours usually combine an end-of-day clean with an in-hours waiting-room and restroom service.
Centers open seven days need weekend coverage planned in advance.

highTouchZones: slit lamps and chin rests (ophthalmology) — exterior surfaces only
protocolSteps: Map each room's specialty equipment and agree which surfaces the clinical team reprocesses per the manufacturer's instructions.
Clean environmental surfaces around the equipment with products compatible with its finishes.
Clean before disinfecting where surfaces are visibly soiled, then hold the label contact time.
Keep procedure rooms on their own cloths and equipment, cleaned last in the room order.
Leave instruments, probes and patient-care devices to clinical staff.
Empty trash; sharps and regulated waste stay with your licensed hauler.
Damp-mop floors, including under procedure chairs.
Log rooms completed and anything the clinic needs to address.
documentationDeliverables: product list with EPA registration numbers and contact times
frequencyGuide: Procedure rooms: environmental surfaces daily, patient-contact surfaces between patients by clinical staff.
Exam and consult rooms: daily.
Waiting areas and restrooms: daily, more often in high-volume clinics.
Floors: daily.
Periodic: walls, vents and high dusting.
vendorQuestions: Which of our equipment surfaces will you clean, and which will you leave to our staff?
Are your products compatible with our equipment manufacturers' cleaning instructions?
How do you sequence a procedure room versus a consult room?
What documentation will you leave after each visit?
How do you train staff on a new clinic's equipment?
scheduleNotes: Specialty clinics usually need after-hours cleaning so procedure rooms are ready for the first case.
Clinics that share space with other practices need the cleaning scope drawn along suite lines.

highTouchZones: pre-op and PACU bay rails and call devices
protocolSteps: Confirm who turns rooms between cases and what the end-of-day terminal clean covers.
Terminal-clean each procedure room after the last case: high to low, clean to dirty, including the entire floor.
Clean lights, booms and equipment exteriors with products compatible with their finishes.
Clean pre-op and recovery bays, curtains on your schedule, and call devices.
Respect sterile processing flow: separate equipment for decontamination and clean areas.
Leave instruments and sterile supplies untouched.
Remove general waste; regulated waste stays with your licensed hauler.
Sign a completion record for every room.
documentationDeliverables: product list with EPA registration numbers and contact times
ATP or fluorescent-marker results when performed
frequencyGuide: Procedure rooms: turnover between cases by the perioperative team; terminal clean after the last case each day of use.
Pre-op and PACU: bays cleaned between patients by staff, full clean daily.
Sterile processing: daily, clean to dirty.
Waiting and restrooms: daily.
Periodic: ceilings, vents and storage areas on a set schedule.
vendorQuestions: What does your terminal clean include, room by room?
How do you respect our sterile processing traffic flow?
Can your crew start after our last case without delaying the next morning?
What completion records will we have for our surveyors?
How do you verify terminal cleaning quality?
scheduleNotes: Terminal cleaning starts after the last case, so crews work evenings on the center's schedule.
Centers with variable case end times need a crew that can start on call.

highTouchZones: treadmill and bike handles and consoles
protocolSteps: Agree which equipment staff wipe between patients and which the cleaning crew handles at end of day.
Clean and disinfect treatment tables and mats with products compatible with vinyl and upholstery.
Wipe down weights, bars and cardio equipment handles and consoles.
Keep gym cloths separate from restroom cloths.
Launder or replace reusable linens per the clinic's process — we do not take clinic linens off site unless contracted.
Empty trash; sharps are rare but stay with the clinic's hauler if present.
Damp-mop gym floors and vacuum carpeted areas.
Log areas completed and any damaged equipment surfaces we notice.
documentationDeliverables: product list with EPA registration numbers and contact times
frequencyGuide: Treatment tables and shared equipment: between patients by staff, full clean daily.
Gym floor: daily.
Restrooms and changing areas: daily or more often.
Waiting room: daily.
Periodic: equipment deep clean and high dusting.
vendorQuestions: Which products will you use on our table upholstery and mats?
Will you clean the free weights and cardio equipment every visit?
What will our staff still need to wipe between patients?
What logs will we receive?
How do you report a torn table cover that can no longer be disinfected?
scheduleNotes: Rehabilitation clinics are typically cleaned after the last appointment, since the gym is in use all day.
Clinics with early-morning patients may prefer a pre-opening clean.

protocolSteps: Agree the daily resident-room clean, discharge cleaning and what nursing staff handle.
Clean resident rooms daily with the resident's dignity and privacy respected.
Discharge-clean rooms after a resident leaves, including all furniture and fixtures.
Clean common areas — dining, activity rooms, corridors — on a set daily schedule.
Follow your infection preventionist's direction during outbreaks, including product changes.
Keep dining-area cleaning coordinated with dietary staff for food-contact surfaces.
Damp-mop floors with attention to fall risk and wet-floor signage.
Record rooms and common areas completed each shift.
documentationDeliverables: product list with EPA registration numbers and contact times
frequencyGuide: Resident rooms: daily, and on discharge or transfer.
Common areas and dining: daily and after meals as directed.
Corridor handrails and elevator buttons: several times a day.
Outbreaks: escalated frequency and products as the infection preventionist directs.
Periodic: floor refinishing, high dusting, vents.
vendorQuestions: How will your staff interact with residents while cleaning their rooms?
What changes in your routine during a norovirus or C. difficile outbreak?
How do you document a discharge clean?
How do you manage wet-floor fall risk in corridors?
Who on your team has bloodborne pathogen training?
How quickly can you add coverage during an outbreak?
scheduleNotes: Skilled nursing facilities need coverage seven days a week, usually during day shift when rooms are accessible.
Discharge cleaning has to fit admission times, so the schedule is agreed with the admissions team.

highTouchZones: resident apartment light switches and door handles
protocolSteps: Agree the housekeeping level in resident apartments, which varies by residence and service plan.
Clean shared areas daily, with extra attention to handrails, elevator buttons and dining rooms.
Enter resident apartments only with permission and at the time agreed.
Coordinate memory-care cleaning with staff so routines and residents are not disrupted.
Escalate cleaning during respiratory or gastrointestinal illness as directed by the residence.
Keep laundry and food-service areas to their own cleaning procedures.
Damp-mop floors with wet-floor signage to reduce fall risk.
Log apartments and common areas completed.
documentationDeliverables: product list with EPA registration numbers
frequencyGuide: Common areas and dining: daily.
Handrails, elevator buttons and shared restrooms: several times a day.
Resident apartments: per service plan, commonly weekly.
Illness outbreaks: escalated as the residence directs.
Periodic: carpets, windows and high dusting.
vendorQuestions: How do your staff behave in a resident's home?
How do you schedule around memory-care routines?
What do you change during a norovirus outbreak?
How do you reduce fall risk while floors are wet?
What records will support our compliance review?
scheduleNotes: Assisted living residences are cleaned during the day, scheduled around meals, activities and residents' preferences.
Apartment housekeeping days are usually fixed so residents know when to expect the team.
